message.content:
Below are three practical ways to grab what’s actually rendered inside **Google Chrome** from a Python script – each one works slightly differently depending on whether you’re willing to restart Chrome yourself, or you prefer a “head‑less” automation tool that does everything under the hood.

| Approach | When to pick it | What you’ll see |
|----------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Playwright** (`playwright`) | You don’t mind opening a fresh Chromium/Chromium‑based browser (or you’re okay with a non‑GUI version). It gives you *exactly* what the engine renders, even off‑screen elements. | Full‑page screenshots, element‑level screenshots, PDFs, video recordings… |
| **Selenium + Chromedriver** | You’d rather stay close to the real Chrome binary and possibly reuse your existing drivers / IDE tooling. Works great when you’re fine with a brand‑new tab/window. | Screenshots of the active tab, optionally cropped to the viewport. |
| **Remote Debugging Port (CDP)** | Your Chrome is already running and you really need to hook into *that exact instance*. Requires you to start Chrome with `–remote‑debugging‑port=` first. | Screenshot of whatever is currently visible in the chosen tab (you can also switch tabs programmatically). |

---

## 1️⃣ Playwright – easiest & most feature‑rich

```bash
pip install playwright
python -m playwright install chromium          # downloads the bundled Chromium
```

### One‑liner demo

```python
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

def main():
    out_dir = Path.cwd() / "screenshots"
    out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    with sync_playwright() as pw:
        # launch a *real* Chromium instance (not head‑less so you can watch!)
        browser = pw.chromium.launch(
            headless=False,                      # change to True for CI environments
            args=["--start-maximized"]           # make sure the window isn’t tiny
        )
        ctx = browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080})
        page = ctx.new_page()

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # 1️⃣ Go somewhere
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        page.goto("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language)")
        page.wait_for_load_state("load")         # waits until DOMContentLoaded
        page.wait_for_timeout(2000)              # give images some extra wiggle room

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # 2️⃣ Take a screenshot
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # • full_page=True → scroll automatically and stitch together
        # • clip={x,y,width,height} → capture exactly the viewport area
        path_full = out_dir / "wikipedia-full.png"
        page.screenshot(path=str(path_full), full_page=True)

        path_viewport = out_dir / "wikipedia-viewport.png"
        page.screenshot(path=str(path_viewport))      # defaults to viewport

        print(f"✅ Saved:\n• {path_full}\n• {path_viewport}")

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # 3️⃣ Clean up
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        browser.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

> ⚡️ Why Playwright?
>
> * Uses the official [Chrome DevTools Protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/) underneath.
> * Handles lazy loading, infinite scrolling, dynamic CSS, etc. automatically.
> * Gives you *pixel‑perfect* screenshots regardless of device pixel ratio (DPR).

---

## 2️⃣ Selenium + Chromedriver – classic, widely supported

Install once:

```bash
pip install selenium webdriver-manager
```

Python snippet:

```python
import time
from pathlib import Path
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager


def save_chromedriver_screenshot(target_url: str):
    """
    Opens a fresh Chrome tab, navigates to ``target_url`` and saves a PNG
    snapshot of the *visible* portion of the page.
    """

    opts = Options()
    opts.add_argument("--disable-infobars")
    opts.add_argument("--no-sandbox")
    opts.add_argument("--log-level=3")
    # Uncomment below if you truly want head‑less mode
    # opts.add_argument("--headless")

    driver = webdriver.Chrome(
        service=webdriver.ChromeService(ChromeDriverManager().install()),
        options=opts,
    )

    try:
        driver.get(target_url)
        driver.maximize_window()
        time.sleep(2)                     # let JS finish rendering

        # Optional: scroll down to trigger lazy loads
        driver.execute_script("window.scrollBy(0, document.body.scrollHeight);")
        time.sleep(1)

        output_path = Path.cwd() / f"{Path(driver.current_url.split('/')[-1]).stem}.png"

        # Save the whole viewport (what you see on screen)
        driver.save_screenshot(str(output_path))
        print(f"[✓] Screenshot saved to {output_path}")
    finally:
        driver.quit()


save_chromedriver_screenshot("https://github.com/")
```

> 📌 Notes  
> * Selenium always launches a *fresh* Chrome instance.  
> * To capture *only* the viewport you simply rely on `driver.save_screenshot()`—it never includes hidden parts of the page.  
> * For a *full‑page* shot you’d need to stitch multiple viewport shots together or use a third‑party helper such as `selenium-stealth` or `browsermob-proxy`.

---

## 3️⃣ Hook into an Existing Chrome Instance (via CDP)

Sometimes you’ve got Chrome already running (maybe you’re testing locally) and you want to snap whatever’s there right now. Start Chrome with a debug port:

```bash
# macOS/Linux
open -na "Google Chrome" --args \
    "--remote-debugging-port=9222" \
    "--app=https://stackoverflow.com/"
# Windows
"C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" ^
    --remote-debugging-port=9222 ^
    --app=https://stackoverflow.com/
```

Now you can talk to that very same Chrome through the DevTools Protocol. Below uses pure Python sockets plus JSON RPC over WebSockets.

First install a lightweight WS wrapper:

```bash
pip install wsproto==1.0.0
```

Full example:

```python
import json
import ssl
import socket
import uuid
import urllib.request
from typing import Dict, Any

WS_URL_TEMPLATE = (
    "ws://{host}:{port}/devtools/browser/{session_id}"
)


class CdpClient:
    def __init__(self, host='127.0.0.1', port=9222):
        self.host = host
        self.port = port
        self.session_id = None
        self.ws_uri = None
        self._connect_ws()

    def _get_session(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Discover available targets."""
        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://{self.host}:{self.port}/json/list")
        return json.loads(resp.read())

    def _connect_ws(self):
        """Open a WebSocket connection to the first available target."""
        targets = self._get_session()
        if not targets:
            raise RuntimeError("No debuggable pages found.")
        self.session_id = targets[0]["id"]
        self.ws_uri = WS_URL_TEMPLATE.format(host=self.host, port=self.port, session_id=self.session_id)

        sock = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port))
        self.ssl_sock = ssl.wrap_socket(sock, do_handshake_on_connect=False)
        self.ssl_sock.do_handshake()

        # Send handshake frame
        key = b'0123456789abcdef'
        header = (
            b'\r\n\r\n\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08\x09\x10\x11\x12\x13\x14\x15\x16\x17\x18\x19\x20\x21\x22\x23\x24\x25\x26\x27\x28\x29\x30\x31\x32\x33\x34\x35\x36\x37\x38\x39\x40\x41\x42\x43\x44\x45\x46\x47\x48\x49\x50\x51\x52\x53\x54\x55\x56\x57\x58\x59\x60\x61\x62\x63\x64\x65\x66\x67\x68\x69\x70\x71\x72\x73\x74\x75\x76\x77\x78\x79\x80\x81\x82\x83\x84\x85\x86\x87\x88\x89\x90\x91\x92\x93\x94\x95\x96\x97\x98\x99\xa0\xb0\xc0\xd0\xe0\xf0\xff'
        )[:8]
        self.ssl_sock.send(header)

    def _send_msg(self, msg: dict) -> int:
        payload = json.dumps(msg).encode()
        length_bytes = len(payload).to_bytes(4, byteorder='big')
        self.ssl_sock.write(length_bytes + payload)
        return len(payload)

    def _recv_msg(self) -> bytes:
        raw_len = self.ssl_sock.recv(4)
        if not raw_len:
            raise EOFError("Connection closed")
        body_length = int.from_bytes(raw_len, byteorder='big')
        body = self.ssl_sock.recv(body_length)
        while len(body) < body_length:
            more = self.ssl_sock.recv(body_length - len(body))
            if not more:
                break
            body += more
        return body

    def send_command(self, cmd_name: str, params=None) -> Any:
        req_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        packet = {"method": cmd_name}
        if params:
            packet["params"] = params
        packet["_id"] = req_id
        self._send_msg(packet)

        while True:
            reply_raw = self._recv_msg()
            reply_json = json.loads(reply_raw.decode())
            if "_id" in reply_json and reply_json["_id"] == req_id:
                return reply_json.get("result")


def screenshot_current_tab(capture_type="viewport"):
    cdp = CdpClient()
    result = cdp.send_command("Page.enable")
    assert result is not None

    # Grab the screenshot
    res = cdp.send_command(
        "Page.captureScreenshot",
        {
            "format": "jpeg",
            "quality": 100,
            "captureBeyondViewport": capture_type != "viewport",
        },
    )
    img_data_base64 = res["data"]

    # Write to disk
    filename = f"screenshot_{capture_type}_{int(time.time())}.jpg"
    with open(filename, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(base64.b64decode(img_data_base64))

    print(f"[✓] Screenshot written to {filename}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screenshot_current_tab(capture_type="viewport")       # or "fullpage"
```

⚠️ **Why this looks complicated**

* The DevTools Protocol speaks over WebSockets, so you either hand‑craft frames or use a ready‑made library (e.g. `pychrome`).  
* In practice you usually won’t write all those low‑level details yourself—you’ll instead use something like [`pychrome`](https://pypi.org/project/pychrome/) or `cdp-py` which wraps the protocol nicely.

---

## Quick cheat sheet

| Task | Code Snippet | Key Points |
|------|--------------|------------|
| **Launch Chrome & screenshot** | See Playwright section above | Head‑less vs GUI, full‑page flag |
| **Capture only viewport** | `driver.save_screenshot(...)` (Selenium) | No stitching needed |
| **Grab a particular element** | `elem.location_once_scrolled_into_view(); elem.size`; `crop_to_rect(screenshot)` | Useful for component tests |
| **Save PDF of page** | `await page.pdf(path="out.pdf")` (Playwright) | Great for printable docs |
| **Automate scrolling** | `while ...: await page.evaluate("scrollBy(...)"` | Needed for infinite lists |

---

## TL;DR

1. **Want a quick, reliable way?** Use **Playwright** – it handles everything behind the scenes and produces perfect screenshots.
2. **Need tight integration with existing test suites?** Stick with **Selenium**, especially if you already ship Chromedriver binaries.
3. **Must work against a live Chrome you didn’t spawn** – start Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and hit the DevTools Protocol (either via a thin wrapper or manual WS handling).

Pick whichever fits your workflow, copy/paste the relevant block, tweak the URL/path, and you’re done! Happy screencapturing 🚀
